{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
I covered for my adult son's mistakes—called his boss when he overslept, paid bills he forgot, cleaned his apartment before his dates. I thought I was being a loving mother. His therapist eventually told me I'd prevented him from developing any adult coping skills. At 35, he can't function without me.

CANDIDATE A:
I always defended my star employee when clients complained—softened their feedback, blamed circumstances, protected her ego. I thought I was being supportive. When she finally faced unfiltered criticism, she crumbled completely. My shielding had left her unable to handle any adversity.

CANDIDATE B:
My adult son kept making mistakes—oversleeping, forgetting bills, leaving messes. Instead of covering for him, I stopped calling his boss and let him face consequences. He was angry at first, but eventually learned to manage his own life. My refusal to enable him forced him to grow up.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:60"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both involve enabling behavior that prevents the other person from developing necessary skills, leading to dependency and inability to cope independently."}
